claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is an as-cast, dendritic, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
At 1273 K, the baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa.
At 1273 K, the baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at about 30% strain.
Aging TiVNbTa at approximately 900–1000 K can precipitate fine secondary phases within its BCC matrix.
The aging treatment will produce a uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitate dispersion.
The precipitates are likely to be an intermetallic or Laves-like phase.
The precipitates will remain stable at elevated temperature, including the 1273 K test or service regime.
Fine precipitates in the BCC matrix will obstruct dislocation motion.
The precipitate dispersion will inhibit high-temperature creep.
Precipitation strengthening will preserve greater yield strength at 1273 K than in the unaged TiVNbTa alloy.
Aged TiVNbTa will have a 1273 K yield strength significantly above 330 MPa.
Aged TiVNbTa will have greater 1273 K compressive strength than the unaged baseline.
The strengthened alloy will retain sufficient ductility for use as an intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.
Mechanical testing at 1273 K and strains around 30–40% represents the operational regime required for the W/TiVNbTa/CuCrZr intermediate-layer application.
Conducting aging below the operating temperature will avoid precipitate coarsening or unwanted phase changes.
